response.justification: Strong, versatile senior engineer with 15+ years of experience, but the profile does not match this role's hard requirements. The position demands native-level Japanese, strong C for UNIX development, Linux kernel source analysis/modification, and embedded LAN-switch security (MACsec, 802.1X, Captive Portal, L2/L3 switching, chip vendor SDKs). The candidate's listed languages are English, Romanian, and basic German — no Japanese at all — and C/C++ work is limited to roughly six months at National Instruments in 2014-2015 plus a university thesis project. The bulk of the last decade is web/backend (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang, AWS) with no networking-protocol, firmware, or kernel-level work. Interviewing would not be a productive use of either party's time unless the Japanese and embedded requirements are negotiable.
strengths: Deep, broad engineering experience (15+ years) with strong testing/CI/craftsmanship discipline
Proven ability to pick up unfamiliar stacks quickly (took over iOS/tvOS app, robotics, DevOps infra)
Some low-level exposure: C/C++ at National Instruments, Linux/JACK audio thesis, high-performance async systems in DLang
concerns: No Japanese language ability — a stated native-level requirement
No embedded networking, switch, or security-protocol experience (MACsec, 802.1X, SNMP, NETCONF)
No Linux kernel analysis/modification; C experience is minimal and over a decade old

key_factors.factor: No embedded/network-security or kernel domain experience
Senior breadth and fast-learning track record
